adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:65 — P2 confidence 100: `a['href'] = "#{prefix}/#{href.sub(/^\/+/, '')}"` rewrites `//cdn.example/path` to the article host's `/cdn.example/path`, while `href.start_with?('/')` leaves `images/photo.jpg` and `../article` relative to the Discourse embed page instead of the source article, breaking imported links and images (the identical image branch has the same defect).

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a bug in the `absolutize_urls` method. Looking at lines 56-66 in topic_embed.rb, the code checks `href.start_with?('/')` which would match both `/path` (root-relative) and `//cdn.example/path` (protocol-relative URLs). For protocol-relative URLs like `//cdn.example/path`, the code would incorrectly rewrite them to `http://eviltrout.com/cdn.example/path` instead of preserving them or converting to `http://cdn.example/path`. Additionally, truly relative URLs like `images/photo.jpg` or `../article` don't start with `/` so they pass through unchanged, but they would be relative to the Discourse page rather than the source article, breaking those links. The same logic applies to the img src handling on lines 67-72.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:37 — P2 confidence 75: `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)` runs outside the post revision transaction and without locking, so concurrent feed/retrieval imports interleaving revision A, revision B, hash B, hash A leave body B paired with hash A and subsequent imports of A skip the required correction.

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real race condition. Looking at the import method in topic_embed.rb, when updating an existing embed (lines 30-37), the PostRevisor.revise! call and embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1) are separate operations not wrapped in a transaction. If two concurrent imports for the same URL interleave (A revises, B revises, B updates hash, A updates hash), the final state could have B's content with A's hash. This would cause future imports of content A to be skipped (hash matches) even though the actual content is B. This is a legitimate concurrency bug in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/tasks/disqus.thor:148 — P1 confidence 100: `post = TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])` makes importing an existing Disqus XML archive depend on fetching every original article, so an unavailable or removed article aborts the archive import instead of preserving its locally available comments as the previous permalink-only creation path did.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that in lib/tasks/disqus.thor, the old code created posts with just a permalink (`raw: "\[[Permalink](#{t[:link]})\]"`) which worked offline with local XML data. The new code replaces this with `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])` which, looking at the TopicEmbed model, calls `open(url).read` to fetch the remote URL content. This means importing a Disqus XML archive now requires fetching each original article URL, and if any URL is unavailable (404, removed, etc.), the import would fail for that thread instead of preserving the comments with just a permalink. This is a real behavioral regression for the Disqus import functionality.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/tasks/disqus.thor:148 — P2 confidence 100: `post = TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])` replaces the category-aware creator while the `--category`/`-c` option is removed, leaving existing category-targeted import invocations without any way to place imported topics into the requested category.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly shows the removal of the `--category` option (method_option :category line is removed) and the replacement of the category-aware PostCreator with TopicEmbed.import_remote which does not accept a category parameter. This means existing scripts or workflows that relied on the `-c` or `--category` flag to place imported Disqus topics into specific categories will silently fail to categorize topics correctly. adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that in the update branch (lines 30-37 of topic_embed.rb), when content_sha1 differs, the code calls `revisor.revise!(user, absolutize_urls(url, contents), ...)` which only updates the post body content, not the title. The `import` method receives a `title` parameter but in the update case, this title is never used - only the content is revised. This means if a publisher corrects their article headline, the forum topic title remains stale. This is a real functional defect in the import logic where title updates are ignored during content updates.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:64 — [P2; confidence 100] `if href.present? && href.start_with?('/')` and `if src.present? && src.start_with?('/')` leave path-relative article links and images such as `related.html` and `images/photo.jpg` unresolved, so imported posts load them from the Discourse origin instead of the source article directory and readers receive broken links and images.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the `absolutize_urls` method in `app/models/topic_embed.rb` only handles URLs that start with '/' (absolute paths). Looking at lines 56-68, the code checks `if href.present? && href.start_with?('/')` for links and `if src.present? && src.start_with?('/')` for images. This means relative URLs like 'related.html' or 'images/photo.jpg' (without leading slash) will not be converted to absolute URLs, leaving them to resolve against the Discourse origin rather than the source article's directory. This is a real bug that would cause broken links and images in imported content.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:3 — [P1/confidence 100] Re-running the already-existing CreateTopTopics migration executes `create_table :top_topics, force: true do |t|`, dropping the populated top_topics table and replacing it with an empty table without preserving its rows or providing a data-restoring rollback.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims that re-running the CreateTopTopics migration would drop and recreate the table. However, looking at the diff, the only change to this file is adding 'force: true' to the create_table call. This is a new migration file (20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb) that creates a new table. In Rails, migrations are tracked and only run once - they don't get 're-run' in normal operation. The 'force: true' option is commonly used in migrations to handle cases where the table might already exist from a failed previous run. This is not a bug that would cause data loss in normal operation, as migrations are idempotent by design through the schema_migrations tracking table.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:50 — [P2, confidence 100] `return if user.blank?` completes retrieval without creating a topic or reporting a configuration error when the configured embedding username is missing or deleted, leaving visitors on the automatically reloading Loading Discussion page indefinitely.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a real issue. In lib/topic_retriever.rb:50-53, the fetch_http method returns silently if the user configured in embed_by_username doesn't exist. Looking at the flow: embed_controller.rb calls Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic) which calls TopicRetriever.new().retrieve, which calls perform_retrieve, which calls fetch_http. If fetch_http returns without creating a topic (because user is blank), the embed/loading.html.erb view will keep auto-refreshing every 30 seconds indefinitely since no topic will ever be created. This is a real bug - silent failure with no error reporting when a required configuration (embed_by_username) points to a non-existent user.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:27 — [P2, confidence 100] `if $redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` records retrieval before `perform_retrieve` succeeds, so a transient fetch failure followed by a retry within 60 seconds makes the retry return normally without importing the topic and consumes that retry as a successful no-op.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a race condition in lib/topic_retriever.rb. Looking at the code: `retrieved_recently?` sets the redis key with `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` and returns false (allowing retrieval to proceed), but this happens BEFORE `perform_retrieve` is called. If `perform_retrieve` fails (e.g., network error in `fetch_http` or `TopicEmbed.import_remote`), the redis key is already set with a 60-second TTL. Any retry within that 60 seconds will have `retrieved_recently?` return true, causing `retrieve` to return early without attempting the import. This is a real bug where the throttle key is set optimistically before success is confirmed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:28 — [advisory, P2, confidence 100] `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)` runs separately after SETNX, so a worker termination between the commands leaves a permanent key that blocks all subsequent nonstaff retrievals for that URL; the strongest rebuttal is the intended 60-second expiry, but no expiry exists until this second command succeeds.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a race condition in lib/topic_retriever.rb lines 26-29. The code uses `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` followed by a separate `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)` call. If the process crashes or is terminated between these two commands, the key will exist permanently without an expiration, blocking all non-staff retrievals for that URL indefinitely. This is a real bug - the atomic SETEX or SET with EX option should be used instead to ensure the key always has an expiration. The diff clearly shows this pattern at lines 26-29 of the new file.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — [P1 confidence 75] `doc = Readability::Document.new(open(url).read,` follows HTTP redirects without revalidating their destinations, so an embed URL on the configured host that redirects to `http://127.0.0.1/` bypasses `SiteSetting.embeddable_host != URI(@embed_url).host`, fetches an internal service from the server, and publishes extracted internal content in an imported topic.

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real SSRF vulnerability. Looking at the diff: 1) TopicRetriever.invalid_host? checks `SiteSetting.embeddable_host != URI(@embed_url).host` only on the original URL. 2) TopicEmbed.import_remote uses `open(url).read` which follows HTTP redirects automatically. 3) If an attacker controls a page on the embeddable_host that redirects to an internal IP (e.g., 127.0.0.1), the host check passes but the actual fetch goes to the internal service. 4) The content is then published via TopicEmbed.import. This is a valid SSRF bypass through open-redirect following.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:26 — [P2 confidence 75] `retrieved_key = "retrieved:#{@embed_url}"` throttles each URL independently after the public controller enqueues retrieval, so an anonymous requester supplying the configured Referer and varying a URL query parameter triggers a fresh full-feed poll and remote fetch per request, exhausting shared job workers and amplifying traffic to the configured site despite the advertised 60-second throttle.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the throttle key in lib/topic_retriever.rb:26 is per-URL (`retrieved:#{@embed_url}`), meaning each unique URL gets its own 60-second throttle. Looking at the flow: EmbedController#best calls Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic) which calls TopicRetriever.new(embed_url).retrieve. The throttle only prevents re-fetching the same exact URL within 60 seconds. An attacker could vary query parameters (e.g., ?foo=1, ?foo=2) to bypass the throttle entirely, triggering fresh poll_feed executions and remote HTTP fetches for each unique URL. This is a real DoS vector where anonymous users can exhaust job workers and amplify traffic to external sites.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:10 — P2 confidence 100: `response.should_not be_success` accepts every non-2xx status in the example named `is 404 without an embed_url`, so an unrelated host rejection or a handled 500 satisfies the claimed missing-parameter contract without proving either the parameter-validation path or the promised status.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the test at line 10 uses `response.should_not be_success` which only checks for non-2xx status, not specifically 404. Looking at the diff, the test claims 'is 404 without an embed_url' but the assertion doesn't verify the specific 404 status code. The controller at line 8 uses `params.require(:embed_url)` which would raise ActionController::ParameterMissing, and the test doesn't verify the exact error handling. This is a valid test quality concern - the test name promises 404 behavior but the assertion is too weak to verify it. However, this is a test precision issue rather than a bug in the application code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb:19 — P2 confidence 100: `SiteSetting.stubs(:feed_polling_url).returns(nil)` and the sibling username example leave `feed_polling_enabled?` at its false default, so both missing-setting tests pass after their respective production guards are deleted because polling already stops at the first condition.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the test file spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb, the test 'requires feed_polling_url' at line 19 only stubs feed_polling_url to nil but doesn't stub feed_polling_enabled? to true. Since feed_polling_enabled? defaults to false (as shown in config/site_settings.yml: 'feed_polling_enabled: false'), the test passes because poll_feed is never called due to the first condition failing, not because of the missing URL. Similarly for the embed_by_username test. This means if someone removes the feed_polling_url or embed_by_username guards from the production code, these tests would still pass incorrectly because feed_polling_enabled? is still false. The finding correctly identifies a real test defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb:35 — P2 confidence 100: `poller.expects(:poll_feed).once` replaces the actual feed-processing method in the sole enabled-feed example, so deleting all RSS parsing and topic imports preserves the entire new poller suite and leaves feed owners without tested import behavior.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the poll_feed_spec.rb test file only tests that poll_feed is called when conditions are met, but never tests the actual poll_feed method implementation. Looking at the diff, the spec at line 35 uses `poller.expects(:poll_feed).once` which mocks out the actual method. The actual poll_feed implementation in app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb (lines 23-38) contains significant logic including RSS parsing, URL extraction, and TopicEmbed.import calls, but none of this is tested. This is a legitimate test coverage gap for newly added nontrivial logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb:34 — P2 confidence 100: `topic_retriever.expects(:retrieved_recently?).returns(false)` and its true counterpart replace the throttle while `topic_retriever.expects(:perform_retrieve).once` replaces retrieval, so a broken Redis expiry, missing staff bypass, or deleted feed-to-HTTP fallback leaves the new retrieval suite green without exercising those lifecycle paths.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the test at spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb:34 mocks `retrieved_recently?` and `perform_retrieve`, which means the actual implementation of throttling logic (Redis setnx/expire in lib/topic_retriever.rb lines 24-31), staff bypass (@opts[:no_throttle] check), and the feed-to-HTTP fallback in perform_retrieve are not exercised by these tests. This is a valid concern about test coverage - the tests verify the control flow but not the actual implementation of these critical paths. However, this is a test coverage gap rather than a bug - the code itself appears correct, but the tests could miss regressions in the throttling or fallback logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb:41 — Advisory P2 confidence 75: `post.cooked.should =~ /new contents/` checks only the returned object's text after an update, so a regression that changes memory without persisting the post or its digest escapes this example and leaves later readers with stale content; the strongest rebuttal is that this is a real model integration test, but it never reloads the post or embed and therefore does not establish durable update behavior.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the test at line 41 in spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb only checks the returned post object without reloading from the database. Looking at the diff, the test does `post = TopicEmbed.import(user, url, title, "muhahaha new contents!")` and then checks `post.cooked.should =~ /new contents/`. This tests the return value but doesn't verify persistence by reloading. However, this is a valid test concern for a model integration test - it should verify the update was actually persisted. The finding is specific, grounded in the diff, and identifies a real gap in test coverage for the new TopicEmbed.import functionality.
